prompt:
A tractor pulls a heavy roller across a field at a constant speed of 2.0 m s^-1. The towbar exerts a pulling force of 3200 N at an angle of 20 degrees above the horizontal.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Diagram showing a tractor pulling a roller along horizontal ground. A towbar tension T = 3200 N acts at an angle of 20 degrees above the horizontal. The roller moves horizontally to the right at constant speed v = 2.0 m s^-1.]
What is the power developed by the tractor on the roller?

answer.explanation: Only the component of force parallel to velocity does work: P = (F cos theta) v = 3200 * cos 20 degrees * 2.0 = 3200 * 0.9397 * 2.0 = 6014 W approx 6.0 kW.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 uses sin 20 degrees instead of cos 20 degrees: 3200 * sin 20 * 2.0 = 2189 W approx 2.2 kW.
Option 2 is correct: P = Fv cos theta = 6014 W approx 6.0 kW.
Option 3 ignores the angle: 3200 * 2.0 = 6400 W = 6.4 kW.
Option 4 divides by cos 20 degrees: 6400 / 0.9397 = 6811 W approx 6.8 kW.
hints: Resolve the force in the direction of motion: F_parallel = F cos theta.
Multiply the parallel force component by speed: P = Fv cos theta.
solution: P = Fv cos 20 degrees = 3200 * 2.0 * cos 20 degrees = 6400 * 0.93969 = 6014 W = 6.0 kW. Option B is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Motion is horizontal, so only the horizontal force component does work.
P = F_horizontal * v = 3007 * 2.0 = 6014 W approx 6.0 kW.
